system.description:
11th Level Clan Feature

It is said that while Chakra was a creation of Shinobi, by Shinobi. Tao is much older and far more primordial in nature. The source of everything in existence, be it living or non-living. Most creatures go their entire lives never knowing Tao or how their lives are shaped by it. But the Yamada have learned to harness it after a botched mission under their homelands shogun. The Yamada now teach and train its more senior members in the ways of Tao, attuning them to one of five base Tao Principles, but unlike others, you have the unique ability to hold any affinity through meditation.

Select one of five Tao attributes gaining its benefits. You can switch this attunement when you complete a short rest.

Wood

When you regain or heal another creatures hit points, increase the amount by half your level, once per creature, per rest.

Additionally, when there are 2 or more hostile creatures within your Executioners Instrument’s range, if you take the Empty Blade attack against one of them, compare your attack result against the AC of up to 2 of them, treating each as if they were the original target.

Fire

You gain 2 ranks of Mastery to your initiative.

Once per turn, when you take the Dash or Disengage actions, you can make an Empty Blade attack with your Executioners Instrument as part of the action taken as if you were forgoing 2 attacks.

Earth

You gain advantage on checks and saves made to resist being moved or knocked prone.

Once per turn, you can forgo one attack granted by the Attack action to guard yourself, reducing the next instance of damage by an amount equal to your [Weapon Damage], before the beginning of your next turn.

Metal

When you roll a d6 as a result of the Empty Blade attack, you can trigger its effect on a 4, 5 or 6.

If you would miss your Empty Blade attack you can spend your Bonus Action to remake the attack.

Water

When a creature attempts to dash, disengage, grapple, disarm, shove or forcefully move you, while they are within your Executioners Instrument range, you can make one weapon attack against them.

Once per turn, when a creature within 30 feet of you attempts to attack an allied creature that is also, within 30 feet of you, you can spend your reaction to move up to your speed, ending it adjacent to your ally and attempting to parry the blow by rolling your [Weapon Damage] die and adding half the result to your allies AC. If the attacking creature misses, you deal your [Weapon Damage] to them.
